Definition: properly, a fixture, i.e. a basis; generally a place, especially as an abode
BiblicalUsage: Makon is the dwelling place, the settled place, the foundation where God abides. Exodus 15:17 calls it the place, O LORD, which Thou hast made for Thee to dwell in, and 1 Kings 8:39 asks God to hear in heaven His dwelling place and forgive. Psalms 89:14 says justice and judgment are the habitation of His throne, and mercy and truth shall go before His face.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word tells me where God lives: not only in a house of stone, but where justice and judgment hold up His throne. My position is that 1 Kings 8:39 is the prayer that goes with it, because the God whose dwelling is heaven still hears from there and forgives.
